newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin shopping mall builder plans ADR issue.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin shopping mall builder plans ADR issue.

text.p: OAO Manezhnaya Ploshchad, the Russian company building an underground shopping centre just outside Moscow's Kremlin walls, plans to issue American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), officials said on Monday.
"We have received a verbal approval from our major shareholder, the Moscow government, and are waiting for a written one," investment department head Maria Kozyreva told Reuters.

She said Manezhnaya Ploshchad was discussing on the ADRs programme with OLMA investment company and Dresdner Kleinwort Benson. She said no details about the level, volume or timing of the issue was decided.
Kozyreva said Manezhnaya Ploshchad was completing its last $30 million share issue, offering 10,000 rouble shares at 12,500 roubles. "The placement is close to an end," she said.

She said the company had previously wanted to make one more share issue, but it had then dropped the plan. "The current issue is big enough and we think we have satisfied demand on the Russian market for the time being," she said.
Manezhnaya Ploshchad is raising funds to build a $330 million shopping mall and says construction will be over by September, Moscow's 850th anniversary.
Kozyreva said most buyers among corporate investors were trading companies which were being excused from six-month deposits if they bought shares for a sum equal to their half-year deposit.
The complex will have 25,000 square meters of trading space and 5,000 square metres for restaurants and cafes and 5,000 square metres for storage.
The company has said it is seeking an average monthly rental price of $2,500 per square metre for retail space and $2,000 for restaurants and cafes.
On the Russian Trading System, a local version of NASDAQ, Manezhnaya Ploshchad was last traded at $2.251 on December 27.
